pool.text: The historic Catholic cathedral in Apia was dedicated on the last day of the year.
Seven warships from Germany, the US, and Britain refused to leave Apia harbour during a typhoon.
Germany ruled Western Samoa as German Samoa with Apia serving as its capital city.
An expeditionary force from New Zealand began the military occupation of German Samoa.
The New Zealand constabulary killed the paramount chief during a peaceful Mau gathering in Apia.
The United States Navy built and operated a naval base in the area.
The modern city of Apia officially became the capital of Samoa.
Apia hosted the Pacific Games for the very first time in the country history.
A magnificent gathering space was designed by an architect and opened in Apia.
The ACC building opened in the city to house several boards and government departments.
The Samoatel building was constructed inland to protect international telecommunications from seasonal cyclones.
Parliament passed an act to better plan for the urban growth of Apia.
The DBS building in Savalalo opened to house the Development Bank of Samoa.
Apia welcomed back the Pacific Games with a massive closing ceremony at Apia Park.
Apia hosted qualification matches for the FIFA World Cup including the first goal.
Apia began hosting the Judo World Cup which later transformed into a regional tournament.
A new courts complex opened in Mulinuu featuring district, supreme, and land and titles courts.
The historic cathedral in Apia was pulled down following severe earthquake structural damage.
The Tui Atua Tupua Tamasese Building opened in Sogi to house government ministries.
Apia hosted an international cricket tournament across the four grounds of Faleata Oval.
